what: Friendface 2 against Tracker Cleaner v1.26 with the cross-site-id counter-repair (C33, M2) fully on. A value detector learns a value is cross-site only after two sites have sent it, so the collector receives the id on first contact and the initial cross-site JOIN happens once and cannot be undone; from then on the cleaner blocks the exact collector path (/f/, never the site root) and strips confirmed ids from URLs and links, so no further send gets through. The trip runs at the fresh-install default (shield C32 off), then measures the fingerprint both ways.
headline: 10/10 kinds joined on first contact (a value detector cannot prevent that); going forward the cleaner stops 4/10 (collector path blocked) and 6/10 survive (first-party server-side, sign-in, per-site cookie, hand-off chain for M3, ETag for M5).
caveats: Lab-only: loopback, made-up names, fake accounts; nothing leaves the machine.

A value-based cross-site detector is reactive: the collector gets the id on first contact, before two sites reveal it is cross-site, so the initial join is not preventable; the cleaner stops every FURTHER send by blocking the exact collector path (never the site root) and stripping the id from request URLs and links.
F4/F5 and F8-to-the-site's-own-server are first-party server-side; they cannot be stopped without breaking the site, so they are marked "cannot", not blocked.
F1 is a per-site first-party cookie (not cross-site) and F7 a sign-in cookie: left alone on purpose. F3 (the hand-off chain) is M3; F10 (ETag) is M5.
The shield (C32) is off by default; the join key (F6 value) is built from fonts/matchMedia/screen (M4). The collector-path block already stops the code reaching the collector.

rows.why: survives: a per-site first-party cookie (fp_id), not a cross-site value: a visited site's own cookie is left alone
stopped going forward: the master id reaches the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
survives: the master id rides the hand-off link under a rotating name; stripping it from a scripted hand-off is M3
survives: the from->to redirect log is the site's own server; cannot stop without breaking navigation
survives: a first-party click record on the site's own server; cannot stop without breaking the site
stopped going forward: the fingerprint code reaches the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
survives: a sign-in cookie (SID): kept on purpose, never touched
stopped going forward: the address and referrer are posted to the collector is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
stopped going forward: the collector runs its loopback probe for the page is blocked (collector-path block, host+/f/ prefix)
